 This Petition, Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Petitioners claiming to be the owners of the subject land are knocking at the doors of Writ Court essentially for a direction to the Respondent-BDA "to allot and re-convey 10 alternate sites at least,
each measuring 60 X 40 sq. ft. in a similar layout".

Learned counsel for the Petitioners vehemently argues that as on the date the Preliminary Notification came to be issued under Section 17(1) of the BDA Act 1976, the name of one Smt.Ithamma widow of Munikonappa was appearing in the Revenue Smt Rajamma vs The Commissioner on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24873076/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Records; neither compensation is paid nor alternate sites have been allotted to the Kathedar or to the successors-in-interest
; instead some alternate sites have been given to one Mr. B.M.Shamanna who was the owner of only 10 Guntas of the acquired 1 Acre & 31 guntas ofland.
Therefore, learned counsel for the Petitioners seeks indulgence of the Writ Court.
2. After service of notice, the Respondent - BDA having entered appearance through its Senior Panel Counsel has filed its Statement of Objections on 19.08.2015, resisting the Writ Petition.

Learned Senior Panel Counsel vehemently submits that: firstly the Writ Petition is highly belated; secondly,
no supportive documents are produced to substantiate the claim of ownership over the lands in question; thirdly, there are civil disputes between Petitioners & other persons; fourthly, sites have already been allotted to as compensatory grants and therefore, now no sites can be given in favour of the Petitioners.
So contending, he seeks dismissal of the Writ Petition.

3. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the petition papers, this Court declines indulgence in the matter for the following reasons:
(a) The acquisition proceedings commenced with the issuance of Preliminary Notification dated 26.04.1978 under Section 17(1) followed by the Final Notification dated 17.11.1982 issued under Section 19(1), of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976.
These Notifications neither contain names of Petitioners nor their predecessors.

To be precise, they mention only the names of Mr. Muniswamy, Mr. S.
Nagappa & Mr. H.M.Shamanna to the extent of 1 Acre & 31 Guntas.

There is no reason to doubt the version of learned Sr. Panel Counsel appearing for the BDA that the award having been passed, the compensation amount has been deposited in the Civil Court way back on 02.12.1987.

Added the issue whether the award is passed or not, would not much matter inasmuch as, there is acquiescence of acquisition from the side of petitioners, who have structured their petition on the basis of acquisition itself.

(b) The vehement submission of learned counsel for the Petitioners that there is enormous culpability attributable to the State & the BDA in commencing &
accomplishing the acquisition proceedings by fraudulently taking the names of third parties, and leaving those of Petitioners who happened to be the true owners of subject land, is bit difficult to countenance.

Adjudicated in a limited jurisdiction constitutionally vested under Articles 226 & 227 vide SADHANA LODH Vs.
NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD., (2003) 3 SCC 524.

SADHANA LODH Vs.
NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD., (2003) 3 SCC 524
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the Petitioners are the true owners of the land in question, is a matter to be debated on the floor of Civil Court where a full fledged trial can take place should a suit be filed by the Petitioners and parties can lead both oral & documentary evidence, as rightly submitted by the learned Panel Counsel appearing for the BDA.
( c) Admittedly, the acquisition proceedings commenced in April 1978 on the issuance of Notification u/s.170 of the 1976 Act followed by the Final Notification dated 07.11.1982.

As already mentioned above, the award is passed way back in the year 1984 which fact can be inferred from the deposit of Smt Rajamma vs The Commissioner on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24873076/
3 compensation amount in the Civil Court although full particulars of the award are not forthcoming from the records here.
Pursuant to the taking of subject land, the BDA has allotted a 40 X 60 site in favour of one Mr. Shamanna whose name figured along with others in the Acquisition Notifications.
Subsequently vide letter dated 20.03.2001 allotment has been made and the Sale Deed has also been executed on 15.06.2001 in his favour as a special case.

The Petitioners had given representations to the concerned seeking allotment of compensatory sites that ultimately resulted into issuance of a negative Endorsement dated 18.11.2013 that is now put in challenge before this Court.

If Mr.
Shamanna was allotted the site way back in June of 2001, the Petitioners ought to have approached the Court soon thereafter.
However, they did it only on 22.03.2014 and no plausible explanation is offered for the long delay brooked.
It hardly needs to be stated that law in general and law of Writs in particular abhors delay.
This is yet another ground as to why no relief can be granted at the hands of this Court.

(d) Learned counsel for the Petitioners relied upon a Co-ordinate Bench decision in B.N.
VEDANAND vs BANGALORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, AIR 1991 KANT 175, wherein some relief was granted to the litigant on the basis of certain facts as discussed in paragraph 8 thereof,
that the compensation was paid to some other persons who were not the khathedars.

sentences.text: However, that is not the case here and therefore, the said decision does not come to the aid of the Petitioners.

The second ruling i.e., BANGALORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY vs SMT. RAMAKKA, 2002 (4)
KCCR 2806, related to re-conveyance of part of developed land in terms of BDA Resolution dated 17.11.1982 which was passed consensually and the same was approved by the Government under the provisions of 1976 Act.

entities.text:

KCCR 2806
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the Co-ordinate Bench acting on the doctrine of promissory estoppel, granted relief to the litigant therein.
Facts of the case thus being much different, no milk can be drawn from this decision, either.

Petitioners reliance on B.K.SRINIVAS vs. BANGALORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, 2009 (4) KCCR SN 180 also does not much come to their aid since the relief was granted to the litigants therein on the basis of a 30 year old promise made by the BDA.

entities.text: B.K.SRINIVAS vs. BANGALORE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, 2009 (4) KCCR SN 180
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, this ruling too does not much support the case of Petitioners.

(e) The above having been said, liberty needs to be reserved to the Petitioners for litigating the matter before the Civil Court inasmuch as, there are some records which indicate that this land was bought by one Mr. Munikonappa vide registered Sale Deed of the year 1945; after his death, his widow Smt. Aithamma appears to have succeeded to the estate along with one son Ramaiah;
Petitioners happen to be the widow & children of said Ramaiah.

The buying of property, succession to the same as per the personal law and consequent claim for alternate sites on that basis, all matters that are to be left for the consideration at the hands of Civil Court.

Added, the cause of action may also avail to the Petitioners as against the said Mr.Shamanna who appears to have obtained the - 10 - Sale Deed allegedly by playing fraud on the BDA and the petitioners who claim to be the true owners of the subject property.
Much cannot be said in that regard since Mr. Shamanna is not a party eo nomine to these proceedings.
Thus, the Petitioners have an alternate & more efficacious remedy to seek redressal of their grievances.
Elsewhere in accordance with law.

In view of the above and with the observations herein above made, this Writ Petition is disposed off.

It hardly needs to be stated that the period spent in prosecuting this writ petition shall be discounted while computing the period of limitation for instituting a suit, b the petitioners before the Civil Court in accordance with law.
All contentions of the parties are kept open.
Costs made easy.
